title: Exceptional inverse image restricts to finite clopen source components
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$, as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ be a finite disjoint open and closed cover, let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be its inclusions [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion], and put $g_i=g\circ j_i$. Use the pro-etale coefficient categories and operations [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the finite-clopen equivalences [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition], finite compact-support direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], and the constructible exceptional inverse images [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

At each finite coefficient level $A=A_{E,n}$, for $K\in D^b_c(X,A)$ with components $K_i=Lj_i^*K$, there is a natural isomorphism
$$
 Rg_!K\simeq\bigoplus_{i\in I}R(g_i)_!K_i.
$$
For every $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ there are natural isomorphisms
$$
 Lj_i^*Rg^!L\simeq R(g_i)^!L.
$$
At finite level they are the right-adjoint comparisons for the displayed direct-sum decomposition. The same comparisons exist on the derived categories of strict etale coefficient systems used to construct the integral exceptional inverse image in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; they commute with evaluation at each level and with the etale/pro-etale system comparison. The integral isomorphisms are their images under restriction of scalars and the derived inverse-limit functor on those actual systems, rather than a choice of a lift of a diagram in an ordinary derived category. The field isomorphisms are obtained by the rationalized and common-stage operations in that definition. For the coefficient unit $\Lambda_Y$ this gives $Lj_i^*\omega_g\simeq\omega_{g_i}$, where $\omega_g=Rg^!\Lambda_Y$ and $\omega_{g_i}=R(g_i)^!\Lambda_Y$. No smoothness, purity orientation, section or tensor invertibility is assumed. Empty components and the empty cover of the empty scheme are allowed.

source.place: Formula C(g,s)=Ls^*Rg^! Lambda_B and its invertibility sentence: finite-clopen compactification and adjunction argument of the earlier split, step 1; coefficient-system construction as specified in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image

proof.text: Choose a compactification $c=(a,p)$ of $g$, with $a:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper. This is legitimate by [thm-nagata-compactification]: a finite-type scheme over a field is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] (a field has only two ideals), hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Put $a_i=a\circ j_i$. Composition of open immersions is open: compose their isomorphisms with open subschemes, whose images remain open. Hence $(a_i,p)$ is a compactification of $g_i$ by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. The schemes $X_i$ are Noetherian opens by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; $j_i$ is quasi-compact, since the inverse image of an affine is closed in that affine and is therefore quasi-compact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes $j_i$ finite type. Its diagonal is an isomorphism, so it is separated. Composing the closed diagonals and concatenating finite lists of algebra generators shows that $g_i$ is separated finite type. The chosen proper part $p$ is the SAME for every $i$. The scheme $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$, since $p$ and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are finite type; [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type] gives a finite bound $d\geq0$ for its dimension when nonempty, as required by the finite adjunction theorem. If it is empty take $d=0$.

source.place: Final invertibility sentence: finite-clopen compactification argument, geometry of the component compactifications

proof.text:
Let $E_i$ be the inverse of the product equivalence [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] applied to the tuple having $M$ in position $i$ and zero elsewhere. In a finite product of additive categories,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_X(E_iM,H)=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(M,j_i^*H),\qquad \operatorname{Hom}_X(H,E_iM)=\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(j_i^*H,M),$$
since all other factors are singleton Hom sets involving zero. Thus $E_i$ is both adjoints of restriction, is exact, and $K\cong\bigoplus_iE_iK_i$. On module sheaves $E_i$ is precisely $j_{i,!}$: [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] makes that functor another left adjoint of the same restriction. The isomorphism is the one whose restriction to $X_i$ is the identity. Exact termwise descent identifies the same functors on complexes and derived categories, as already specified in the clopen equivalence.

source.place: Tag 04TS, lemma-mapping-property-glue; elementary finite-product Hom calculation using the cited derived equivalence

proof.text:
For the chosen compactifications, $a_!E_i\cong(a_i)_!$. Indeed, on sheaves the two functors are left adjoint to $j_i^*a^*=(a_i)^*$, using [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to the identity of these right adjoints, with opposite categories, to obtain the unique unit-compatible isomorphism. Both extension functors are exact by [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact], so termwise application and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descend that comparison and its inverse. Consequently [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed] gives $Rg_!E_i\cong Rp_*(a_i)_!=R(g_i)_!$. The functor $Rp_*$ is a right adjoint by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; it preserves a finite product since maps into that product are tuples of maps under its adjunction bijection. Finite products are biproducts here, so it also preserves finite direct sums. Apply $Rp_*a_!$ to the decomposition in Step 2 to obtain
$$Rg_!K\cong\bigoplus_iR(g_i)_!K_i.$$
All maps are natural in $K$. On bounded constructible inputs the comparison with any originally chosen compactifications is [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]; these inputs have etale origin by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], so this use stays in its asserted domain.

source.place: Tags 03DI and 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero and lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; finite compact-support formula and elementary biproduct calculation

proof.text:
For $M\in D^b_c(X_i,A)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,A)$, use Step 2, Step 3 and [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] to obtain natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{X_i}(M,j_i^*Rg^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(E_iM,Rg^!L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rg_!E_iM,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(R(g_i)_!M,L).$$
Here $E_iM$ is bounded constructible by the clopen equivalence, hence of etale origin. The functors $Rg^!$ and $R(g_i)^!$ have bounded constructible values by the specified constructible restriction in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. For each $L$, both objects therefore represent the same functor of $M$ on the full category $D^b_c(X_i,A)$. The uniqueness argument of [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] applies: transpose the counit in each direction and evaluate the Hom identities at the two representing objects; the two composites are identities. Naturality of the Hom bijections gives naturality in $L$. This produces a natural isomorphism $\rho_i$, uniquely specified by
$$\varepsilon_{g_i,L}\circ R(g_i)_!(\rho_{i,L})=\varepsilon_{g,L}\circ Rg_!(c_{i,Rg^!L})\circ b_{i,j_i^*Rg^!L}^{-1},$$
where $c_i:E_ij_i^*\to\mathrm{id}$ is the product adjunction counit and $b_i:Rg_!E_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R(g_i)_!$ is Step 3. This equation identifies the comparison as the component right-adjoint comparison of the direct-sum formula, rather than an arbitrary isomorphism.

source.place: Final invertibility sentence: component identification of the dualizing object, by the finite compact-support adjunction

proof.text: Now work with strict etale systems $\mathsf S_A$ of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. The cover identifies $X$ with $\coprod_iX_i$: maps on the disjoint open components glue uniquely, and gluing the component inclusions gives inverse scheme maps. The etale clopen decomposition [lem-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-clopen-product] extends to constant-$A_n$ modules: transport each scalar action and each linearity equation componentwise through its fully faithful equivalence. Apply this at every $n$; a transition is a family of component maps and its semilinearity equation is checked on each component. This gives an exact product equivalence for STRICT systems with inverse given by zero insertion and finite products, and with evaluation $e_n$ commuting with restriction and insertion. Exactness and inverse identities are levelwise. The exact functors induce derived functors by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Their unit and inverse identities descend by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Thus on derived systems, insertion $E_{i,A}$ and restriction $r_{i,A}$ are adjoint in both orders, with the same zero-component Hom calculation as Step 2; the termwise units and counits descend and retain their triangle identities. In particular this is an equivalence of actual derived system categories, not a product decomposition of the evaluations of an unspecified diagram.

source.place: Tag 0A5B, lemma-constant-smooth-statements, finite disjoint-union paragraph; coefficient-system extension using levelwise actions and transitions

proof.text:
Write $F_{g,A}=Rp_{A,*}a_{!,A}$ and $F_{g_i,A}=Rp_{A,*}(a_i)_{!,A}$ as in [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint], for the common proper part of Step 1. There is an isomorphism
$$b_{i,A}:F_{g,A}E_{i,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{g_i,A}.$$
To construct it, apply [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] at every coefficient level to $a\circ j_i$. The isomorphism commutes with transitions: on the extension-by-zero presheaves both orders send a section on the component to that same section on its image, with its coefficient action restricted along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$, and send the other summands to zero. Sheafification preserves these equalities by its universal property. These are therefore inverse maps of strict systems, natural in the system, not independently chosen derived level maps. Exactness of open extension holds levelwise by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; descend its comparison by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] and apply the actual functor $Rp_{A,*}$. No interchange of evaluation with a chosen resolution is needed here. Evaluating $b_{i,A}$ gives the corresponding ordinary etale finite-level comparison by [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison].

source.place: Constructions 5.14–5.15 and Lemma 5.16, printed p. 35; clopen case with the same proper part, using Stacks 03DH/03DJ

proof.text:
Let $G_{g,A},G_{g_i,A}$ be the actual right adjoints supplied by [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]. Step 5 and Step 6 give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,r_{i,A}G_{g,A}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E_{i,A}M,G_{g,A}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{g,A}E_{i,A}M,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{g_i,A}M,N).$$
By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] this constructs a natural isomorphism $\rho_{i,A}:r_{i,A}G_{g,A}\cong G_{g_i,A}$ IN the derived category of strict systems. Its defining counit equation is exactly Step 4's equation with system subscripts. Evaluation respects $b_{i,A}$, the product adjunction, and the units/counits of $F\dashv G$ by [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]. Thus evaluation of that equation is the finite etale equation; uniqueness of its transpose identifies $e_n\rho_{i,A}$ with the finite-level right-adjoint comparison. This also proves the transition compatibility with the prescribed adjunction mates. It does not infer equality of system maps merely from equality at all evaluations.

source.place: Right adjoint after Lemma 5.16 and Lemma 5.22, printed pp. 35–36; component comparison by the explicit Hom bijections

proof.text:
The etale/pro-etale comparison respects this construction on actual systems. The square $j_i^*
u_X^*\cong
u_{X_i}^*j_i^*$ is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. It extends to systems termwise: all maps are natural in coefficient-module morphisms, so they commute with the strict transitions; exactness permits derived descent by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. The system comparison and evaluation of $R
u_{Y,A,*}$ are those of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. Whisker Step 7 by $R
u_{Y,A,*}$ and $
u_{X_i,A}^*$, using the preceding square. This gives
$$r_{i,A}
u_{X,A}^*G_{g,A}R
u_{Y,A,*}\cong
u_{X_i,A}^*G_{g_i,A}R
u_{Y,A,*}.$$
Evaluation gives $Lj_i^*Rg_n^!\cong R(g_i)_n^!$. The comparison is the one of Step 4: [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] identifies the extension terms, and [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] states that the transported Hom bijections respect compactification comparisons. Therefore transporting the counit equation of Step 7 gives exactly Step 4's equation. Uniqueness in [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identifies the two maps. This proves the asserted site and evaluation compatibility, within bounded-below etale-origin domains when using the finite pro-etale adjunction.

source.place: Finite-clopen component comparison together with the actual system construction specified in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image

proof.text:
For an integral $L$, compose the system isomorphism of Step 8 with the reduction functor $\mathcal R_Y$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. This is an isomorphism $r_{i,A}\mathcal T_gL\cong\mathcal T_{g_i}L$ of actual derived strict systems. Restriction of scalars $DU_X$ commutes with $r_{i,A}$: both underlying systems have the restricted component sheaves and the same transitions and completed-ring actions. The clopen equivalence [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] says that restriction also commutes with derived inverse limits and finite reduction. Apply the functor $R\lim\circ DU$ to this system map, with the total-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The formula $Rg^!_{\mathcal O_E}=R\lim\,DU_X\mathcal T_g$ in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] now yields
$$Lj_i^*Rg^!_{\mathcal O_E}L\cong R(g_i)^!_{\mathcal O_E}L.$$
Here $\mathcal T_g$ and $\mathcal T_{g_i}$ are formed, as the definition permits, with the compactifications $c=(a,p)$ and $c_i=(a_i,p)$ of Step 1. The integral $Lj_i^*$ agrees with component restriction: by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], $Lj_i^*K=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_nj_i^{-1}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$, since finite-level pullback along $j_i$ is termwise restriction. The clopen equivalence commutes restriction with reduction, $\operatorname{Res}_n$ and $R\lim$, so this is $j_i^{-1}R\lim_nK_n$; for $K=Rg^!_{\mathcal O_E}L$, derived complete by its $D^b_c$ typing, $K\cong R\lim_nK_n$ [def-weil-derived-complete]. Invertibility follows because a functor sends an isomorphism and its inverse to mutually inverse maps. No reconstruction of a morphism from unrelated maps in ordinary derived categories has occurred.

source.place: Integral coefficient-system clause: apply the actual derived inverse-limit functor to the system comparison

proof.text: These isomorphisms are $\mathcal O_E$-linear, since the system adjoints and all restriction/extension maps are linear. Rationalization therefore sends the comparison and its inverse to mutually inverse $E$-linear transformations, using exactly [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]'s rationalized functors. For a finite extension $E\subset E'$, the scalar comparison for $G$ is an isomorphism of systems, including the cofinal indexing comparison, by [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]. It commutes with the component comparison: coefficient extension commutes with restriction and zero insertion, and the two composites of open extension send every local section to the same extended section. Transposing these squares gives the same right-adjoint square by the pasting identities [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; hence the two orders of scalar comparison and $\rho_i$ coincide, including their system morphisms. The coherent scalar comparisons pass through $DU$ and $R\lim$ by the construction in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Thus the $E$-comparisons agree after every common finite extension and define the asserted natural isomorphism in the common-stage $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ category. This uses the actual systems' scalar comparisons, not just an equality of their evaluated objects.

source.place: Construction 5.15 and Lemmas 5.16/5.22, plus the finite-free scalar construction recorded in lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint; rationalized/common-stage descent is as in def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image

proof.text: Take $L=\Lambda_Y$. By definition [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], $Rg^!\Lambda_Y=\omega_g$ and $R(g_i)^!\Lambda_Y=\omega_{g_i}$, giving $Lj_i^*\omega_g\cong\omega_{g_i}$ at all four stages. If $X_i$ is empty its module category and system category have only the zero object, so $E_i=0$ and every displayed component isomorphism is the unique zero-to-zero map. If $I$ is empty, the cover condition makes $X$ empty; the product decomposition of [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition] makes $K=0$ and Step 3 gives $Rg_!K=0$, the empty direct sum. There are then no restriction comparisons to assert. The argument nowhere uses smoothness, an orientation, a section, or tensor invertibility.
